_purpose: Sharpening pass following the v0.1.1 epistemic repair. Universally applies the epistemic status taxonomy, adds explicit promotion conditions for every translation hypothesis, and defines the continuous accessibility functional D_O explicitly so that the collapse-rate formalism in Section 5.3 and Section 6.1 becomes well-posed.
_global_invariant: Every claim in PHYS-CORE-014 must carry an explicit epistemic status from the taxonomy {A_definition, B_classical_or_source_result, C_derived, D_translation_hypothesis, E_prediction_or_conjecture}. Every D_translation_hypothesis must carry a promotion condition specifying what would be required to promote it to C_derived. Every continuous-collapse statement must use D_O; every structural-collapse statement must use dim(ℳ_C^O).

epistemic_status_taxonomy.A_definition: Definition internal to NSFG or adopted from an explicitly cited source.
epistemic_status_taxonomy.B_classical_or_source_result: Result actually established in the cited mathematical source.
epistemic_status_taxonomy.C_derived: Mathematical consequence derived from definitions and already-established results, with all required hypotheses shown.
epistemic_status_taxonomy.D_translation_hypothesis: Proposed NSFG-to-classical or classical-to-NSFG correspondence whose analytic equivalence has not yet been independently established.
epistemic_status_taxonomy.E_prediction_or_conjecture: Claim proposed by NSFG that requires a new proof, construction, or empirical/mathematical validation.

content.collapse_statement_rule: Continuous collapse laws must be written in terms of D_O. Structural collapse states must be written in terms of dim(ℳ_C^O). The two symbols are not interchangeable.
content.inequality_direction_rule: Every inequality must carry the exact direction required for each downstream implication. Upper bounds may not be used as lower bounds.
content.domain_rule: Every estimate must state the domain (ℝ³, 𝕋³, bounded subset, weighted Sobolev space). Estimates valid on bounded domains do not transfer to ℝ³ without additional decay or localization hypotheses.

add_subsection.title: Definition of the Continuous Accessibility Functional D_O

definition.informal: D_O is a nonnegative continuous functional measuring the degree to which the observer-relative accessible quotient admits distinguishable continuations. D_O > 0 corresponds to a non-degenerate accessible reality; D_O = 0 corresponds to the proposed collapse state.
definition.formal_candidate: D_O(h,x,t) := ∫_{ℳ_C^O(h,x)} w_O(q) dq, where w_O: ℳ_C^O(h,x) → ℝ_{≥0} is an observer-relative weight function assigning nonnegative accessibility weight to each accessible equivalence class, and the integral is with respect to a measure on the accessible quotient. The weight w_O and the measure are required to be invariant under the observer's coherence relation ∼_O.
definition.alternative_candidate: D_O(h,x,t) := |{ [q] ∈ ℳ_C^O(h,x) : w_O(q) ≥ I_N(O) }|^{1/2}, a normalized count of distinguishable equivalence classes above the observer's resolution threshold, raised to a fixed power to permit a continuous collapse law.
definition.selection_criterion: The final form of D_O is to be selected so that: (i) D_O = 0 if and only if ℳ_C^O(h,x) is empty or all its elements are below the observer's resolution threshold; (ii) D_O > 0 if and only if at least one element of ℳ_C^O(h,x) is distinguishable; (iii) D_O admits a continuous collapse law under the scaling hypotheses of Section 5.3.

properties: Structural correspondence: D_O = 0 if and only if ℳ_C^O(h,x) = ∅ or all elements of ℳ_C^O(h,x) are below I_N(O).
Structural correspondence: D_O > 0 if and only if dim(ℳ_C^O(h,x)) > 0 (under the structural definition of dimension).
Observer-relative invariance: D_O is invariant under the observer's coherence relation ∼_O.
Continuity: D_O is continuous in h and x on the domain of admissible observer-relative references.

relation_to_dimension.statement: D_O and dim(ℳ_C^O) are related but not identical. D_O is a continuous functional; dim(ℳ_C^O) is a structural/topological quantity. The two agree at their zeros: D_O = 0 if and only if dim(ℳ_C^O) = 0. They need not agree in their positive values; D_O measures degree of accessibility while dim(ℳ_C^O) counts dimensions.
relation_to_dimension.collapse_law: Continuous collapse laws are stated as D_O ≍ τ^γ. Structural collapse states are stated as dim(ℳ_C^O) = 0. The two statements are related by the boundary condition D_O = 0 ⇔ dim(ℳ_C^O) = 0.

_final_handoff.instruction: PHYS-CORE-014 v0.1.2 concludes with: (i) a universal epistemic status taxonomy applied to every claim; (ii) promotion conditions on every translation hypothesis; (iii) falsification conditions on every prediction; (iv) an explicit definition of the continuous accessibility functional D_O in Section 9.2.6; (v) a canonical distinction between continuous collapse (D_O) and structural collapse (dim(ℳ_C^O)); (vi) all bridge obligations B1–B3 identified with promotion conditions in Section 4.6.
_final_handoff.preserved_invariant: The Library remains the NSFG substrate. Coherence remains observer-relative and domain-dependent. The OpenAI manuscript remains the source of the classical construction, not a validation of its NSFG interpretation.
_final_handoff.new_construction: A fully annotated, machine-readable epistemic architecture in which every claim's status, promotion condition, or falsification condition is explicit, and in which continuous and structural collapse quantities are cleanly distinguished.
